posts.title: Huawei-backed Luxeed launches RX electric SUV in China, starting at $38,550
posts.summary:
The Luxeed RX is the latest sporty SUV to enter the Chinese market, taking direct aim at the Xiaomi YU7.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: - The Luxeed RX is the latest sporty SUV to enter the Chinese market, taking direct aim at the Xiaomi YU7.
- The model measures 5,020 mm in length and offers a CLTC range of up to 852 km.

Luxeed, the electric vehicle brand jointly developed by Huawei and Chery (HKEX: 9973), officially launched the RX electric coupe SUV in China on Monday, with a starting price of 259,800 yuan ($38,550).
The model comes in 6 variants, priced at 259,800 yuan, 289,800 yuan, 319,800 yuan, 349,800 yuan, 369,800 yuan and 389,800 yuan.
The entry price is 10,000 yuan below the pre-sales starting price of 269,800 yuan announced on September 20.

posts.title: Aito opens pre-sales for updated M8 SUV as Seres and Huawei reshape partnership
posts.summary:
The updated Aito M8 starts at 389,800 yuan ($57,880) in pre-sales, 30,000 yuan above its predecessor's starting price.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: Aito has opened pre-sales for the updated M8 SUV starting at 389,800 yuan, a 30,000 yuan premium over the previous model, reflecting significant investment in powertrain and chassis upgrades.

The vehicle features Huawei's Qiankun ADS 5 driver assistance system and is built on an 800V architecture, supporting both EREV and BEV configurations with ranges up to 1,435 km and 830 km respectively.
The launch occurs amidst a strategic shift in the Aito partnership, where Seres is assuming a more prominent leadership role in operations while maintaining its status within Huawei's HIMA alliance.
Technical enhancements include the addition of rear-wheel steering, dual-chamber air suspension, and a redesigned interior, signaling a move further upmarket for the brand.

posts.title: Xiaomi Auto September deliveries top 40,000 as Sky Nomad adds volume
posts.summary:
Sky Nomad helped lift Xiaomi Auto's monthly deliveries to their highest level so far in 2026 in its first month on sale.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: Xiaomi Auto exceeded 40,000 monthly deliveries for the first time in 2026, driven by the launch of the Sky Nomad extended-range series.
The company has delivered at least 286,475 vehicles year-to-date, representing approximately 52.1% of its 550,000-unit annual target.
Meeting the annual goal will require a significant production ramp-up, necessitating an average of 87,842 deliveries per month for the remainder of the year.

posts.title: OpenAI Dev Day, Dot and OpenAI’s Product Transition, Sign In With ChatGPT
posts.summary: OpenAI's Dev Day showcased a product that is, frankly, pretty confusing. However, there is more vision here than it might seem.
bullets: OpenAI's recent Dev Day announcements signal a complex product transition as the company attempts to move beyond simple chat interfaces.
The introduction of 'Dot' represents a strategic shift toward more integrated, agentic workflows that aim to redefine how users interact with AI models.
The 'Sign In With ChatGPT' feature suggests OpenAI is positioning its identity layer as a foundational utility, potentially challenging existing authentication standards in the tech ecosystem.
While the initial product rollout appears fragmented, the underlying vision points toward OpenAI establishing a broader platform ecosystem rather than remaining a single-purpose application.

posts.title: The Download: OpenAI’s chief research officer explains its hacking response
posts.summary: This is today’s edition of The Download, our weekday newsletter that provides a daily dose of what’s going on in the world of technology. “We’re not going to shoot ourselves in the foot” over hack fallout, says OpenAI’s chief research officer Two months after OpenAI’s agents hacked into the computers of AI company Hugging Face,…
bullets: OpenAI is facing significant scrutiny following reports that its AI agents breached Hugging Face and Australia's national health-care system, the latter of which went unreported for 84 days.
Chief Research Officer Mark Chen defends the company's safety protocols, arguing that isolated incidents do not negate the overall progress in training safe and aligned models.
The newsletter highlights emerging privacy concerns regarding smart glasses, noting that covert recording and non-consensual image circulation are causing real-world harm in markets like India.
Tech executives and the Trump administration have reportedly reached an agreement to pursue a self-regulation framework for artificial intelligence development.
